comparator.name: Computing Science
comparator.sourceNotes: The programme-specific 2026-2027 TER defines one 180-EC English-language Computing Science curriculum. Years one and two each contain 60 EC of compulsory courses. Year three contains 30 EC of compulsory research, security and distributed-systems work plus a genuine 30-EC free minor. The minor remains open rather than being filled with an invented student choice.

alternatives.concept: Builds a computing programme around programming, networks and operating systems, databases, software development, algorithms and mathematical foundations, with data and AI applications. It captures substantial Groningen Computing Science content while retaining UCR's interdisciplinary structure rather than claiming the full specialist architecture, security and capstone sequence.

alternativeSelection.assessment: All generator-eligible interests form one coherent Computing Science programme spanning software, algorithms, systems, security, data, modelling and mathematical foundations. The supporting topics strengthen that same closest match, while the search-only examples and outcomes do not generate a second organising direction. A second UCR curriculum would therefore be a relabelled near-duplicate rather than a substantively different programme.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Introduction to Programming directly addresses programming fundamentals and computational problem solving, with different language, scope and credits.
Logic & Discrete Mathematics directly addresses formal logic for computer science, with different scope and credits.
Algorithms & Data Structures directly addresses algorithm and data-structure design, though not specifically through C.
Advanced Algorithms directly addresses the advanced-algorithms component, with different scope and credits.
Probability & Statistics directly addresses probability and statistical foundations, with different scope and credits.
Mathematical Methods supplies calculus and related mathematical foundations, with different scope and credits.
Linear Algebra directly addresses the comparator component, with different scope and credits.
Computational & Numerical Methods extends calculus computationally but does not reproduce the full Calculus 2 syllabus.
UCR combines logic and discrete mathematics in one selected course, so no second UCR course is aligned to this separate component.
UCR has no selected dedicated computing-science research-skills course.
Networks & Operating Systems directly addresses computer networks, while also covering operating-system concepts.
Database Management Systems provides a core information-systems technology, with narrower database-centred scope.
Software Development addresses design, testing and maintenance, though Groningen's component is larger.
Consumer Product Design provides iterative design practice but does not reproduce a disciplinary introduction to computing science.
UCR has no selected course that reproduces the compulsory computer-architecture component.
Introduction to Programming includes object-oriented programming, but UCR has no second selected course for this separate Groningen component.
UCR has no selected course that reproduces the separate advanced-programming component.
Software Development uses Haskell, but UCR has no second selected course for the separate functional-programming component.
UCR has no selected dedicated web-engineering course.
Networks & Operating Systems covers this field, but it is already aligned to Groningen's separate Computer Networks component.
UCR has no selected course that reproduces the languages-and-machines component.
UCR addresses responsible technology but has no selected technical information-security course.
UCR has no selected dedicated distributed-systems course.
UCR's optional independent-research opportunity is shown separately against the compulsory 15-EC Bachelor Project; it is not part of the fixed 180-EC UCR programme.
The genuine 30-EC free minor is preserved without inventing a Groningen minor selection.
Image Processing & Computer Vision addresses visual computing, but not the full graphics-and-visualization scope.
Machine Learning directly addresses the introductory machine-learning component, with different scope and credits.
